blocks.text: The Algoma Substance Abuse Rehabilitation Centre has a rich history of providing a safe and supportive environment for women seeking recovery from chemical dependency. Founded in the early 1980s, this rehabilitation centre evolved from a local chapter of Women for Sobriety into a fully operational recovery home for women. With funding secured from the Ministry of Health and contributions made by the Federal Government, the United Way of Sault Ste. Marie and other community supporters, the agency was able to purchase property and establish Breton House in 1986.

centre.about_html:
General Information

Breton House is a residential facility that is specifically designed to support women aged 19 years and over who are seeking to make positive changes regarding their substance use. The facility offers six to eight beds, and residents can look forward to participating in groups both at Breton House and within the community. The facility also offers access to 12-Step meetings. 

Breton House is a scent-free and smoke-free zone, with a special designated area for smoking outside. The safety of all residents is paramount, and as such, the facility maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards drug and alcohol use on the premises, as well as toward violent threats or actions. 

Mission & Vision

Breton House’s mission is straightforward: to support women with substance abuse issues in achieving better health and truly becoming empowered, with opportunities for both growth and change. Meanwhile, the Breton House vision is one of empowering hope, allowing women to seize control of their lives and take positive strides forward, leaving substance abuse behind.

Admission Criteria

Prospective residents will need to undergo a provincial assessment, with the results faxed to Breton House. Once the assessment is evaluated, prospective residents will be contacted at their provided number. If out of town, an initial interview will be conducted over the phone, or in person if residing in the area. This intake process is designed to assess potential residents’ needs and gather necessary information. To gain admission, prospective residents must have addiction-specific issues. 

Key Points

Breton House maintains a no-smoking, no-scent policy. Additionally, all medications must be in properly labeled containers and mood-altering medications are considered on a case-by-case basis. Residents who are on methadone or suboxone will be required to be on a stable dose; specific information relevant to methadone and suboxone can be discussed with staff during the initial intake process. 

Overall, Breton House provides specialized support for women seeking to make positive strides forward in their lives. Its evidence-based treatment options, emphasis on community involvement, and zero-tolerance policies combine to create a nurturing environment that promotes growth and change.

 

Breton House - Center Overview

The Algoma Substance Abuse Rehabilitation Centre has a rich history of providing a safe and supportive environment for women seeking recovery from chemical dependency. Founded in the early 1980s, this rehabilitation centre evolved from a local chapter of Women for Sobriety into a fully operational recovery home for women. With funding secured from the Ministry of Health and contributions made by the Federal Government, the United Way of Sault Ste. Marie and other community supporters, the agency was able to purchase property and establish Breton House in 1986.

The centre’s mission is to offer opportunities for women to grow and change in their pursuit of recovery from addiction. The centre is governed by a volunteer board of directors chosen from the community for their qualifications and skills to ensure policy-setting and governance of the programs are of a high standard, while the staff implements and provides the service delivery of the programs. Today, the Algoma Substance Abuse Rehabilitation Centre continues to provide a safe, structured and supportive environment for women seeking recovery from chemical dependency, going beyond treating addiction itself, the centre looks at uncovering the underlying issues that have led to the addiction to give the clients the best chance for a sustainable recovery.

raw_html:
General Information

Breton House is a residential facility that is specifically designed to support women aged 19 years and over who are seeking to make positive changes regarding their substance use. The facility offers six to eight beds, and residents can look forward to participating in groups both at Breton House and within the community. The facility also offers access to 12-Step meetings. 

Breton House is a scent-free and smoke-free zone, with a special designated area for smoking outside. The safety of all residents is paramount, and as such, the facility maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards drug and alcohol use on the premises, as well as toward violent threats or actions. 

Mission & Vision

Breton House’s mission is straightforward: to support women with substance abuse issues in achieving better health and truly becoming empowered, with opportunities for both growth and change. Meanwhile, the Breton House vision is one of empowering hope, allowing women to seize control of their lives and take positive strides forward, leaving substance abuse behind.

Admission Criteria

Prospective residents will need to undergo a provincial assessment, with the results faxed to Breton House. Once the assessment is evaluated, prospective residents will be contacted at their provided number. If out of town, an initial interview will be conducted over the phone, or in person if residing in the area. This intake process is designed to assess potential residents’ needs and gather necessary information. To gain admission, prospective residents must have addiction-specific issues. 

Key Points

Breton House maintains a no-smoking, no-scent policy. Additionally, all medications must be in properly labeled containers and mood-altering medications are considered on a case-by-case basis. Residents who are on methadone or suboxone will be required to be on a stable dose; specific information relevant to methadone and suboxone can be discussed with staff during the initial intake process. 

Overall, Breton House provides specialized support for women seeking to make positive strides forward in their lives. Its evidence-based treatment options, emphasis on community involvement, and zero-tolerance policies combine to create a nurturing environment that promotes growth and change.

 

Breton House - Center Overview

The Algoma Substance Abuse Rehabilitation Centre has a rich history of providing a safe and supportive environment for women seeking recovery from chemical dependency. Founded in the early 1980s, this rehabilitation centre evolved from a local chapter of Women for Sobriety into a fully operational recovery home for women. With funding secured from the Ministry of Health and contributions made by the Federal Government, the United Way of Sault Ste. Marie and other community supporters, the agency was able to purchase property and establish Breton House in 1986.

The centre’s mission is to offer opportunities for women to grow and change in their pursuit of recovery from addiction. The centre is governed by a volunteer board of directors chosen from the community for their qualifications and skills to ensure policy-setting and governance of the programs are of a high standard, while the staff implements and provides the service delivery of the programs. Today, the Algoma Substance Abuse Rehabilitation Centre continues to provide a safe, structured and supportive environment for women seeking recovery from chemical dependency, going beyond treating addiction itself, the centre looks at uncovering the underlying issues that have led to the addiction to give the clients the best chance for a sustainable recovery.
